Host and parasite cultures Media Infected and uninfected host cultures were maintained in F/2 medium (Guillard’s Marine Water Enrichment Solution, Sigma), using filtered and autoclaved natural seawater from the Penzé estuary collected in June one year before at the 27 of salinity and stored at dark. After preparation, the medium was complemented with 5% (v/v) soil extract (Starr and Zeikus 1993). A final filtration using a 0.22 µm pore size filter was processed under sterile conditions. Stock cultures conditions All stock cultures were maintained at 19°C and on a L:D cycle of 12:12 h at 80 µEinstein m2 s−1. Stock culture of the host is produced using non-ventilated flasks by transferring the host culture into fresh medium (ratio 1:1) every 3-4 days. Stock cultures of the parasite were propagated using 10mL culture flasks, by transferring 300 µL of infected host culture into 3mL of exponentially growing uninfected hosts every 3-4 days. Scrippsiella acuminata ST 147 Host culture Inoculate the host culture (J3-J4) in fresh media in ventilated flasks by transferring 3/4 of media and 1/4 of host growing exponentially. Transferring should be done every Monday and Friday to maintain and increase the host culture volume. Incubate at 21°C, light 12:12. Parasite Amoebophrya culture Inoculate the parasite culture (J3-J4) by transferring 1/10 of parasite culture in host J3-J4 culture. Seeding every Monday and Friday to maintain and increase the culture volume. Incubate at 21°C, light 12:12.

steps.title: Collect and fix cytometry samples
steps.instruction: Take 1 ml from each flask at each time point (T0, J1 before/after filtration, J4 before/after filtration) into cryotubes, add 10 µl of 1 % glutaraldehyde/pluronic (10 µl per 1 ml sample), incubate 5 min at 4 °C in the dark, then store tubes at –80 °C; later analyse by flow cytometer for Scrippsiella (natural fluorescence) and for dinospores and bacteria after SyBr Green DNA staining.

steps.title: Filter dinospores and start infection culture
steps.instruction: Observe host (Scrippsiella) and parasite (Amoebophrya) cultures by epifluorescence microscopy (450 nm blue filter) to ensure dense, exponentially growing host and abundant, swimming dinospores. Install sterile filtration funnels on vacuum flasks, place a PC 5 µm filter, and filter the Amoebophrya culture by gravity (max 150 ml per filter); replace saturated filters and autoclave discard. Verify absence of host cells microscopically (optional). Pool all filtrates. In a 600 ml ventilated flask add 300 ml host culture and 150 ml pooled filtrate (ratio 1 vol dinospores : 2 vol host) and incubate at 21 °C with a 12 h : 12 h light cycle.

steps.title: First 10 µm filtration to remove bacteria
steps.instruction: At the appropriate infection stage (26 h after mixing for strain A25 or 15 h for A120), prepare 200 ml fresh‑media flasks for rinsing. Install sterile funnels, place a nylon 10 µm filter, and filter the culture by gravity (max 125 ml per filter). Using an ethanol‑cleaned tweezer, transfer the filter to a 50 ml centrifuge tube, rinse the filter with fresh medium using a P1000 pipette, and discard the filter in an autoclave bag. Optionally examine the filtrate microscopically to confirm few host cells.

steps.title: Second 10 µm filtration and medium addition
steps.instruction: Repeat the 10 µm filtration on the previously collected infected host cells: set up a new sterile funnel with a nylon 10 µm filter, filter by gravity, rinse the filter with fresh medium, and collect the cells in a centrifuge tube. Add ~100 ml fresh medium to each funnel to wash out remaining bacteria; if the filter saturates, split the sample and use another filtration system. Discard the used filter in an autoclave bag. In each 600 ml ventilated flask add 350 ml fresh medium, then add the 30 ml of infected and cleaned Scrippsiella cells, and bring the total volume to 400 ml.

steps.title: Add antibiotics and incubate culture
steps.instruction: Add 20 ml of PNS 100× stock to each 400 ml culture to obtain a final PNS concentration of 5× (antibiotic cocktail). Incubate the cultures at 21 °C with a 12 h : 12 h light cycle. Keep the PNS stock at –20 °C and bring it to 4 °C before use.

steps.title: Purify parasite culture via 3 µm filtration
steps.instruction: Three days after bacterial removal, examine the culture by epifluorescence microscopy (450 nm) to confirm abundant dinospores and few host cells. Install sterile funnels, place a PC 3 µm filter, and filter by gravity (max 100 ml per filter, one filter per system). For a 420 ml flask use four separate filtration systems; pool all filtrates. Distribute 2 × 3 ml of each pooled filtrate into a 6‑well plate for microscopy; if any host cell is observed, re‑filter the sample with a new sterile system. Finally, pool all filtrates from the same original flask.

steps.title: Collect parasite fraction for RNA (Trizol)
steps.instruction: In a chemical hood, add 4 ml Trizol to each 15 ml Falcon tube, wrap in aluminum foil, keep on ice. Install sterile funnels with a PC 0.6 µm filter, split the pooled filtrate into two portions (~200 ml each) and filter using a vacuum pump at <100 mm Hg, stopping before the filter dries. Fold each filter and place it into the corresponding Trizol‑containing tube, mix by hand for 1–2 min, flash‑freeze for 5 min, then store at –80 °C. Complete both filtrations within 15 min to avoid RNA degradation.

steps.title: Collect parasite fraction for genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Install sterile funnels with a PC 0.6 µm filter and split the pooled filtrate into two portions (~200 ml each). Filter by gravity, assisting with a hand pump if needed. Place the first filter into a labeled 15 ml Falcon tube on ice while the second filtration finishes; then place the second filter into the same tube (or, if filtration exceeds 30 min, place each filter in a separate tube). Flash‑freeze the tube(s) and store at –80 °C. Optionally, dinospores can be pelleted by centrifugation at 11 000 rpm for 20 min at 18 °C in 50 ml Falcon tubes.
